question: A community garden starts the season with 85 tomato seedlings planted. A spring donation adds 59 more seedlings. A second donation adds 76 more seedlings. The seedlings are then split evenly among 4 garden plots, and only one plot's share is tracked from here. That plot gains 39 more seedlings from a greenhouse, delivered in 60 minutes, or exactly one hour. Finally, 56 more seedlings are added to that plot from a late planting. How many seedlings does that plot have now?

A movie theater starts the evening with 213 seats booked. Then 48 seats are cancelled due to a scheduling change. The remaining bookings are split evenly among 5 screens, and only one screen's bookings are tracked from here. A doubling promotion doubles that screen's bookings. Finally, 27 more seats are booked for that screen from a walk-up line. How many seats are booked for that screen now?

A dairy farm starts the morning with 135 gallons of milk collected, on a property that also raises 20 unrelated chickens. By midmorning, 12 more gallons are collected. A cooperative order then multiplies the total by 4. The milk is split evenly among 6 delivery trucks, and only one truck's load is tracked. Finally, 58 gallons from that truck are delivered to a local creamery, a delivery that takes 40 minutes, well under an hour. How many gallons of milk does that truck have left?

A brewery starts the batch with 163 gallons of beer fermenting, in a facility that also has 40 unrelated wine barrels in storage. A large order multiplies the batch by 8. Then 32 more gallons are added from a second tank. Another 7 gallons are added from a top-up. A distributor deal then multiplies the batch by 7. A doubling of the batch happens when a second distributor places a matching order. Finally, 9 more gallons are added from a final adjustment. How many gallons of beer does the brewery have now?

In the morning, a shoe store has 235 pairs of sneakers in stock, in a mall that also has 20 unrelated pretzel stands. By midday, 36 more pairs arrive from a shipment. In the afternoon, 124 pairs are sold during a sale. By late afternoon, 51 more pairs arrive from a second shipment. By evening, 49 more pairs arrive from a final delivery. How many pairs of sneakers does the store have now?

A classroom terrarium starts the week with 19 crickets for the class lizard, in a room that has kept pets for a dozen years, unrelated to today's count. On Monday, 17 crickets are fed to the lizard. On Tuesday, 1 more is fed. A new shipment then multiplies the remaining crickets by 6. Finally, 5 more crickets are fed to the lizard on Wednesday. How many crickets are left in the terrarium?

A print shop starts the day with 110 flyers printed. By midmorning, 25 more are printed. By midday, 63 more are added. A citywide campaign then multiplies the whole batch by 9, a run that takes 90 minutes, or an hour and a half. Then 21 more flyers are printed for a late order. Finally, 10 more are printed as extras. How many flyers does the shop have now?

A textile mill starts the week with 87 bolts of fabric woven, in a factory that also has 40 unrelated sewing machines on order. A wholesale order multiplies the bolts by 3. A second wholesale order multiplies them by 7. A third order triples the batch once more. Then 5295 bolts are shipped out to a garment factory. The remaining bolts are split evenly among 6 storage racks, and only one rack's share is tracked. Finally, a distributor bonus multiplies that rack's bolts by 9. How many bolts of fabric does that rack have now?

In the morning, a construction site has 239 bricks stacked. By midday, 59 more bricks arrive. In the afternoon, 105 bricks are used to build a wall. By evening, a supplier bonus multiplies the remaining bricks by 5, a delivery that takes 120 minutes, or two hours. Finally, 52 bricks are used for a final section. How many bricks are left on site?

A comic book store has 89 back issues of a rare series in stock. A doubling of the stock happens when a second store's inventory is merged in for a joint sale. Then 54 issues are sold during a convention. A distributor deal then multiplies the remaining issues by 9. Finally, a second distributor deal multiplies the stock by 5. How many back issues does the store have now?

A stamp collector named Iris has 73 stamps, compared to her rival Owen's collection of 40 stamps kept in a binder that also holds 15 unrelated coins. Iris trades away 69 stamps at a swap meet. She then buys 50 more stamps from a dealer. She receives 31 more stamps as a gift. Finally, a rare-find bonus multiplies her whole collection by 8. How many stamps does Iris have now?

In the morning, a bakery has 201 loaves of bread, in a shop that also sells 20 unrelated pastry boxes. The loaves are split evenly among 3 delivery routes, and only one route's load is tracked from here. By midday, 40 more loaves are added to that route from a second batch. In the afternoon, 54 more loaves are added. By evening, a wholesale order multiplies that route's loaves by 5. Finally, 191 loaves are delivered to fulfill a restaurant order. How many loaves does that route have left?

Zara has 159 dollars in a shared vacation fund with her cousin Milo, whose own savings hold 90 dollars separately. She deposits 55 more dollars from a paycheck. She adds 14 more dollars from a refund. She then splits the fund evenly with Milo, keeping only her half. A matching bonus multiplies her half by 5. Finally, she adds 57 more dollars from a bonus at work. How many dollars does Zara have now?

Lucia has 23 dollars in her craft fund, less than her friend Yara's 90 dollars, kept in a box that also holds 15 unrelated buttons. She earns 64 more dollars selling bracelets. She earns another 46 dollars from a custom order. She spends 89 dollars restocking beads and thread. Finally, she earns 58 more dollars from a weekend market. How many dollars does Lucia have in her craft fund now?

In the morning, a parking garage has 238 empty spaces, in a building that has operated for half a century, unrelated to today's count. By midmorning, 33 spaces fill up. By midday, 40 more spaces open up as early commuters leave. In the afternoon, 171 spaces fill up during a downtown event. By evening, 32 spaces open up. Finally, 41 more spaces open up as the event ends. How many empty spaces does the garage have now?

A toy drive starts with 83 toys collected. A weekend donation adds 34 more toys. A doubling match from a corporate sponsor doubles the whole collection. Then 23 more toys arrive from a school collection. Afterward, 146 toys are delivered to a children's hospital, a delivery that takes 90 minutes, or an hour and a half. Finally, 33 more toys arrive from a late donation. How many toys does the drive have now?

A recycling club starts the week with 26 pounds of aluminum collected, in a school that has run environmental clubs for a dozen years, unrelated to today's total. On Tuesday, 15 more pounds are collected. On Thursday, 16 more pounds are collected. A citywide drive then multiplies the total by 4, a weigh-in that takes 30 minutes, or half an hour. Finally, a matching donation multiplies the total by 4 again. How many pounds of aluminum does the club have now?

Liam had $19 saved in his piggy bank after doing chores that took him 120 minutes, or 2 hours, over the week. He spent $16 of it on a new comic book at the corner store. His grandmother then doubled whatever money he had left as a reward for his good grades. After that, the bus fare home cost him $1. Finally, he earned $45 walking dogs over the weekend, more than his friend Noah, who earned just $20 that week from his paper route. How much money did Liam have after walking the dogs?

Grandpa collected 167 eggs from the hen house early in the morning. By midday, the hens had laid 30 more eggs, which he added to the crate. In the afternoon, he sold 20 eggs to a neighbor. Later that afternoon, 10 more eggs turned up in a nest he'd missed. By evening, a second flock delivered 73 more eggs to the crate. How many eggs did Grandpa have in the crate by evening?

Sophie started her lemonade stand with $42 in the cash box, which is 4200 cents. During a summer fair, first five nearby stands and then eight more identical stalls each pooled in an amount equal to what she currently had, growing her cash box to five times, and then eight times, its size. Unfortunately, she had to pay $1,451 to replace a broken cooler and canopy. A generous donor then added $73 to the box. The fair organizers split the remaining shared fund evenly between her stand and one partner stand, so she kept half. Finally, she paid $94 in rent for the stall space. How much money did Sophie end up with?

Jason had 116 baseball cards in his binder. He traded away 2 cards for a rare rookie card. At a card show, eight other collectors each brought a set exactly equal to what Jason had, and they combined collections, making Jason's share nine times as large, even though the show had 300 vendors set up that day. He then had to give up 403 cards to pay off a bet he lost. Finally, he won 48 more cards in a raffle, ending up with far more than his friend Marcus, who only had 90 cards. How many cards did Jason have at the end?

In the morning, Mr. Kim counted 119 fish in his display tank, out of the 30 tanks in his shop. By midday, 72 fish had been sold to customers. In the afternoon, he added 29 new fish from a delivery. A wholesaler then offered a deal where three tanks just like his were combined, tripling his fish count. Later that afternoon, 67 more fish arrived from a rescue shelter. By evening, a final delivery made his total six times as large. How many fish did Mr. Kim have in his tank by evening?

Sam packed 68 apples for a group hiking trip. Along the trail, 52 more apples were added from a farm stand they passed. At base camp, three other hiking groups combined their apple supplies equally with Sam's, making the total four times as large. That evening, 38 more apples were donated by a passing trail crew. Finally, 40 more apples arrived with the last group to reach camp. How many apples were in the group's supply by the end?

Priya's bike shop had 218 bikes in stock at the start of the month. A small supplier delivered 6 more bikes. She then sold 58 bikes during a weekend promotion. A big shipment brought in 80 more bikes. A merger with a partner store, matching her stock exactly, doubled her total inventory. A second matching shipment then doubled it again. By month's end she had far more bikes than her rival Diego, whose shop only held 300 bikes. How many bikes did Priya's shop have at the end of the month?

Wendy filled a candy jar with 128 pieces of candy for a party, worth 12,800 cents in total value at the store's pricing. She added 23 more pieces from a bulk bag. A second bag added 56 more pieces. A latecomer guest brought 16 more pieces to contribute. A candy exchange with two other party tables, each matching the jar's count, made the jar's total three times as large. Finally, 16 more pieces were added from the leftover party favors. How many pieces of candy were in the jar at the end?
